newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz calls for equality in EU bid.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz calls for equality in EU bid.

text.p: New Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz has asked European Union leaders to treat Turkey's bid for EU membership equally with those of other candidate countries, his office said on Thursday.
Yilmaz made the call in a letter to EU Commission President Jacques Santer and EU leaders, expressing Turkey's commitment to seek full membership and "concerns" about the fate of its bid.

"We believe in the right of Turkey to benefit to the same extent as the other candidates from the strategy being developed for countries seeking full membership," Yilmaz said in the letter, distributed by his office.

Yilmaz said signs of equal treatment would support Turkey's effort to overcome obstacles to membership -- commonly seen as a poor human rights record, a troubled economy and disputes with EU member Greece.
"If this is not the case, it will be clear that the statements made by the EU in recent months are not backed by the resolve of concrete measures," the statement said.
Turkey is one of 12 countries awaiting a July 16 European Commission judgement on how suitable each is for full membership.
Analysts say Turkey's chances of quick membership are slim but that Europe does not want to marginalise the pro-Western nation, with a population of 60 million in a strategic location.
Many in Turkey, a Moslem but secular nation, feel Europe is reluctant to accept them because of religious and cultural differences.
Secularist leader Yilmaz took office last week following months of political chaos which led to the collapse of the previous Islamist-led coalition in June.
His left-right coalition vowed to seek full EU membership in its government programme, set to be debated in parliament on Thursday ahead of a vote of confidence on Saturday.
The government programme promised rapid harmonisation of laws to ease a customs union between Turkey and the EU which went into effect at the start of last year.
